title: Structured Domain Values Left as Raw Strings Beyond Their Parsing Boundary
pattern: Structured domain data remains primitive text inside the domain: a multi-part identifier is kept as a concatenated string when its components have domain meaning; business logic extracts properties by raw string operations (slicing, splitting, regex matches); or constrained formats such as emails, phone numbers, postal codes, URLs, and IP addresses lack a type preserving their required validation guarantees.
why_bad: Domain behavior becomes coupled to raw encoding conventions rather than typed properties and invariants. Consumers must duplicate parsing or validation, trust undocumented upstream checks, or risk silently misinterpreting malformed values. Format changes become scattered across the business logic.
detection: Subcase A (composite identifiers and extraction): substring, `.split()`, `.find()`, slicing, or regex-capture operations that extract semantic properties from an identifier or encoded value within domain services. A single extraction is enough; repetition is not required. Subcase B (constrained formats): internal `String`/`&str` struct fields or function parameters representing genuinely constrained formats (emails, phone numbers, zip codes, URLs, IP addresses) whose construction does not enforce and preserve validity in the representation. This subcase needs no extraction or splitting. Semantic names like `email`, `url`, `ip`, `phone` are leads, not proof; identify the actual grammar, component semantics, or domain validity requirement before reporting.
counterexample:
Parsing raw JSON payloads, command-line strings, or encoded identifiers at the system boundary (e.g., HTTP controllers or DTO translation layers). Formatting a composite identifier solely at the boundary for logging or rendering to the UI. Free-text comments, descriptions, biographies, or address fields where any arbitrary Unicode input is valid:
```rust
struct UserSession {
    profile_bio: String,
}
```
Opaque IDs that the domain never decomposes need not expose invented components; if a separate validity contract exists, it still needs enforcement.
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (p. 190); *Refactoring* by Martin Fowler (p. 84, 144); *Domain Modeling made Functional* (p. 75, 110); *A Philosophy of Software Design* by John K. Ousterhout (p. 45); *Building Secure and Reliable Systems* by Heather Adkins et al. (Chapter 6, p. 115-116).
